methodological_rigor.justification: Solid diagnostic accuracy study with dual-reader blinding, ICC=0.992 demonstrating excellent inter-observer agreement. Appropriate ROC/DeLong testing for model comparison. Single-center retrospective design limits causal inference. ROI placement rigorous with exclusion of necrosis/hemorrhage.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Diagnostic accuracy study comparing novel APTw biomarker to standard PI-RADS. Incremental improvement modest (0.875 to 0.915 AUC). Clinically relevant for risk stratification but not paradigm-shifting. Gray-zone analysis demonstrates practical utility.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive Methods including MRI acquisition parameters, image processing, post-processing standards. Complete Results with AUC, sensitivity, specificity reported. Minor: STARD checklist adherence could be explicit. Data availability statement absent.

novelty_literature.justification: APTw application to PCa diagnosis is novel; combination with PI-RADS incremental. Establishes APTw as complementary biomarker but mechanism previously described in gliomas. Addresses documented gap in understanding APTw utility in prostate cancer but confirms expected biological rationale.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear Methods and Results sections. Figures 2-5 effectively communicate diagnostic performance and clinical utility. Discussion contextualizes findings appropriately. Writing precise and technically sound throughout.

key_strengths: Excellent inter-observer reliability (ICC=0.992) with dual-reader blinding and consensus protocol
Rigorous subgroup analyses addressing clinically relevant scenarios (transition zone, PSA gray zone)
Appropriate statistical comparison (DeLong test) demonstrating incremental diagnostic value
Representative cohort of 160 patients with confirmed pathology (86 PCa, 74 BPH)
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with potential selection bias; no external validation
Incremental improvement modest (4% AUC gain); clinical significance unclear for routine adoption
APTw signal is mixed contrast influenced by pH and MT effects; absolute protein quantification not achieved
No prospective validation or multi-vendor assessment reported
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically sound diagnostic study establishing APTw as complementary biomarker. Dual-reader blinding and rigorous subgroup analysis strengthen evidence. Incremental improvement over PI-RADS modest. Requires external validation before clinical implementation. Tier 3 appropriate.
